issues.legal_issue: A Hindu widow may surrender her estate in favour of the reversioners even after a stranger has acquired title by adverse possession against her.
material_facts: A stranger had remained in possession of the deceased husband's property long enough to acquire title by adverse possession against the widow.
The widow later executed a deed surrendering her widow's estate in favour of the husband's nearest reversioners.
issues.conclusion: The surrender was not invalid or inoperative merely because the stranger had already acquired title against the widow; the reversioners could claim as heirs of the last male holder.
issues.legal_principle: A widow's surrender is a voluntary self-effacement that extinguishes her interest and opens succession to the husband's heirs; it is not a transfer of title from the widow. Rights acquired against the widow do not bind the husband's heirs. The Court relied on Gounder v. Gounden, Vytla Sitanna v. Mariwada and Mumareddi v. Pitti Darairaja, and approved Ram Krishna v. Kausalya and Raghuraj Singh v. Babu Singh; it disapproved Subbamma v. Subrahmanyam, Sundrasiva v. Viyyamma, Arunachala v. Arumuga, Lachmi v. Lachho and Basudeo v. Baidyanath.

predicates.claim_by_reversioners_after_widow_surren: The proceeding involves reversioners claiming the deceased husband's property after the widow surrendered her estate in their favour.
predicates.stranger_acquired_adverse_title_against_: A stranger acquired title to the property by adverse possession against the widow.

issues.definition: When reversioners claim after a widow's surrender and a stranger acquired title against the widow, the surrender does not prevent the reversioners from claiming as heirs.

issues.legal_issue: A widow's surrender is an act of self-effacement that opens succession by operation of law, rather than a transfer requiring acceptance by the reversioners.
material_facts: The widow executed a deed surrendering her interest in her deceased husband's property to the nearest reversioners.
The reversioners claimed the property as heirs of the last male holder.
issues.conclusion: The reversioners derived their title from the last male holder, and the estate vested in them by operation of law without any act of acceptance.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Hindu law doctrine of surrender, the widow's complete self-effacement has the legal consequence of her death for succession purposes. The reversioners take as heirs of the last male holder, not as transferees from the widow; surrender and acceptance are not matters of contract. The Court relied on Gounder v. Gounden and the principles stated in Vytla Sitanna v. Mariwada and Mumareddi v. Pitti Darairaja, and explained that the legal consequences are not materially different from those of a widow's adoption of a son.

predicates.widow_surrendered_estate_to_reversioners: The widow voluntarily surrendered her estate in favour of the reversioners.
predicates.claim_based_on_succession_to_last_male_h: The reversioners claim the estate as successors of the last male holder.

issues.definition: When a widow surrenders her estate to reversioners who claim as successors of the last male holder, the estate vests in them by operation of law without their acceptance.

issues.legal_issue: Reversioners may recover possession from a person whose adverse possession was against the widow immediately after her surrender, without waiting for the widow's death.
material_facts: A stranger acquired title by adverse possession against the widow and remained in possession of the property.
The widow surrendered her estate to the next heirs of her deceased husband while she was alive.
The reversioners sued to recover possession from the stranger.
issues.conclusion: The reversioners were entitled to recover possession immediately as heirs of the last male holder and were not required to wait until the widow's death.
issues.legal_principle: Because surrender extinguishes the widow's interest and opens succession, the reversioners take in their own right as heirs; adverse possession against the widow does not defeat their claim. The Court observed that the legal consequences of surrender are not materially different from those of adoption. It approved Ram Krishna v. Kausalya and Raghuraj Singh v. Babu Singh and disapproved Subbamma v. Subrahmanyam, Sundrasiva v. Viyyamma, Arunachala v. Arumuga, Lachmi v. Lachho and Basudeo v. Baidyanath.

predicates.claim_for_possession_by_reversioners_dur: Reversioners seek possession of the deceased husband's property while the widow is still alive.
predicates.widow_surrendered_estate: The widow surrendered her estate in favour of the reversioners.
predicates.adverse_possession_was_against_widow: The possessor acquired title by adverse possession against the widow, rather than against the reversioners.

issues.definition: If reversioners seek possession during the widow's lifetime after her surrender and the adverse possession was against her, they may recover without waiting for her death.

issues.legal_issue: Equitable conditions on reversioners' recovery after a widow's surrender do not protect trespassers who acquired title by adverse possession against the widow.
material_facts: The possessors entered the land as trespassers without any right.
They later acquired title through adverse possession against the widow.
The widow surrendered her estate to the reversioners, who sought possession during her lifetime.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming a court may impose equitable conditions on recovery in an appropriate case, no equitable consideration justified delaying the reversioners' recovery from these trespassers.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assumed, without deciding, that equity, justice and good conscience might permit conditions on a reversioner's right to recover during a widow's lifetime to prevent prejudice to interests created by the widow. That possibility did not assist persons who entered as trespassers; the law of limitation had legalised their usurpation, and their title against the widow was not enforceable against the reversioners. The Court distinguished persons who take a transfer from a widow and referred to the general principles discussed in the conflicting authorities, including Ram Krishna v. Kausalya and Raghuraj Singh v. Babu Singh.

predicates.claim_by_reversioners_after_widow_surren: The proceeding involves reversioners seeking possession after the widow surrendered her estate.
predicates.possessor_entered_as_trespasser: The possessor entered the land without any right or title.
predicates.possessor_acquired_title_against_widow_b: The possessor later acquired title by adverse possession against the widow.

issues.definition: When reversioners seek possession after surrender from a person who entered as a trespasser and acquired title against the widow by adverse possession, equity does not delay their recovery.
